confusions: The Who pays page's 46.0% is a share of all taxes paid, not a share of income, and I nearly took it for a tax rate until I found the small note under it.
On the Who pays page I could not tell whether a figure was for Income Tax alone or for all taxes, and I had to read the two sections to work it out.
The defence NATO figure is set out in a long note under the table, and I had to read through the sources to find the 2025 number.
I could not find the OECD structural reform figures anywhere on the site, and the OECD sources list does not mention them, so those questions are not sure.
I could not find house prices, mortgage rates, first-time buyers, welfare history or the state pension anywhere, and I went round many pages for nothing.
The 1992 employment figures for the 18 to 24 and 25 to 34 year olds are not there, because the age chart starts in 2008.
On the manifesto pages the Back button takes me to the Questions list and not to the table of promises, so I lost my place every time and had to start again.
The answer about why productivity stops at 2021 is tucked under Limits near the bottom of the page, and I nearly read the wrong year off the chart.
Many of the figures are hidden in More on or Show boxes that I had to open one at a time, which slowed me down a lot.
The long pages with lots of charts made it hard to keep track of where I was, and I could not always tell how far down I had got.
